sources.author: William Lilly
sources.title: Christian Astrology
sources.read_mode: Original engraved/typeset 1647 page images direct visual examination; not modern transcription

source_rules.source_summary: Partill is when the actual planetary positions form the same number of degrees as a perfect traditional aspect; sign-degree examples include Venus at ninth degree Aries and Jupiter ninth degree Leo; and exact conjunction examples.
source_rules.operationalization: Matching integer numbered degree of signs separated by classical traditional non-conjunction aspect rays; source-language proxy, not automatically exact continuous angular residual.
source_rules.missing: minute-level boundary convention/forceful contact and whether 1 degree tolerance is warranted

source_rules.source_summary: Platick aspects within the moities of the orbs of both involved planets, illustrated by Venus 10° and Saturn 18° in appropriate signs; p110 repeats half each orb example.
source_rules.operationalization: angular distance to nearest conjunction/ray must be at most half the sum of the two planets' printed orb widths. For joined Moon/Mercury use physical longitudinal conjunction; for seeing-by-ray, separately use sign aspect and orb-near exact ray.
source_rules.missing: Lilly's CVII p536 uses joined without declaring one table selection or luminosity fortification; do not silently replace with 3/5/10° engineering orbs.

source_rules.source_summary: Lilly explicitly lists alternative orbs among authorities and notes that he himself sometimes uses different entries.
source_rules.status: Two componentwise extremes encoded; mixed combinations are bracketed but not individually enumerated.

source_rules.source_summary: A planet occupying the sign ascending or an intercepted sign is principal significator and one with dignity there participates; more than one in the horoscope can be significators.
source_rules.missing: Difference between ascending sign and actual historical quadrant first house/horoscope remains.

source_rules.source_summary: In absence of planet in the ascendant seek planets joined to Moon or Mercury, giving special consideration if the same joined both and weighing comparative power.
source_rules.missing: What qualifies luminaries/Moon-Mercury mutual joining when unfortified and whether plurality governs; numerical priorities unresolved.

source_rules.source_summary: When first two conditions fail, consider lord of ascendant conditional on its dispositor beholding it by some aspect.
source_rules.missing: When Ascendant lord is in its own domicile, the dispositor is the same body; must not call its own self aspect qualified.

source_rules.source_summary: If aspect to Ascendant lord fails, seek a planet forcibly and partilely aspecting Moon and Mercury.
source_rules.missing: Ambiguity of and/or, which planet is forcibly strong, and whether source defines a numerical one-degree tolerance.

source_rules.source_summary: Last named fallback is whichever planet possesses most essential dignities at the Moon/Mercury places, followed by fixed stars.
source_rules.status: NOT_IMPLEMENTED; remaining unattributed circumstances counted only.
source_rules.missing: full source term/triplicity/dignity arbitration and competing planetary strength.

allowed_public_data: Source-neutral full-century geometric aggregate count and distinct HD state coverage only; no personal source chart or respondent outcomes
same_instant_ptolemy_conditional_four_mo: 4,553 timestamps as already source-verified; all historical variants and contested interpretation remain unresolved
